problem_statement: When a TSCH node that uses Orchestra scheduling keeps a primary link together with a backup link reserved for reception, the node can miss its reception window and lose packets. This is most pronounced when the node's primary link has no packet to send and it must decide between the primary link and the backup link, and when more than one candidate link is available. The observable symptom is that the node fails to acknowledge some packets: its link statistics report a transmit count that does not equal the acknowledged count, instead of the near-total (essentially 100%) acknowledgment rate expected on an error-free radio link. The expected behavior is that the node operates the appropriate link in these situations so that every transmitted packet is acknowledged and the network reaches the expected acknowledgment rate.
causal_chain: The affected unit is the Cooja scenario 26-cooja-rpl-tsch-orchestra-perfect-link.csc, which builds the simple-node example for a two-node RPL/TSCH network with Orchestra scheduling (link-based Orchestra, storing routing and link-stat packet counters enabled) over a UDGM perfect radio link. Its ScriptRunner waits for the node's 'Link Stats' output and asserts that the transmit count (tx) is greater than zero and equals the acknowledged count (ack), so a passing run requires tx == ack. Under the unfixed base behavior the node's decision of which link to operate does not correctly handle the case where the primary link has no packet to send, so it can operate a link that misses the reception window; packets are then not acknowledged, tx differs from ack, and the test fails. After the production fix the node selects the link consistently, the reception window is met, all transmitted packets are acknowledged, and tx == ack, so the test passes.

verification.reason: The original statement identifies the symptom and area well but leaves the required backup-link selection behavior ambiguous; these gaps can be repaired by clarifying the observable expected behavior without giving implementation details.

problems.detail: The statement says the node should operate the 'appropriate' link when more than one candidate link is available, but does not specify that the backup link should be the highest-priority candidate link reserved for reception.

The fix can be exercised when the currently selected link itself has Rx capability but no packet to send; the statement does not clearly require switching to a higher-priority backup link in that case.
The test scenario is run with link-based Orchestra enabled, while the statement only mentions Orchestra scheduling in general.

leak_check.leak_detail: The new statement adds the exact scheduling/switching logic from the fix: the backup link should be the highest-priority RX candidate, and the node should switch to it when the current link has no packet even if the current link also has RX capability, provided the backup link has higher priority. This closely mirrors both changed code conditions and reveals a substantial part of how to solve the task.

verification.auto_status: review: no fix passed the checks
